title: Capacity reserve trigger and scope-defer decision matrix
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: We repeatedly overshoot cycle commitments when unplanned infra work or incidents absorb engineering capacity, forcing late scope cuts and stakeholder churn. Goal: create an operational decision matrix that defines a small, experimentable capacity reserve (buffer) and a clear, repeatable scope-defer rubric so PMs and Eng leads can make fast, aligned trade-offs mid-cycle. Scope: one-cycle pilot across infra-facing, console, and SDK initiatives. Success metrics: fewer emergency scope cuts (target <=1 per initiative), median time-to-decision for scope deferral < 24 hours, and maintainted OKR velocity >= 85% of committed points on non-emergency work.
decisions: Reserve policy: hold a soft reserve equal to 10% of committed cycle capacity (measured in story points) per cross-functional pod for the pilot.
Trigger: reserve is unlocked automatically if 3 consecutive business days show team burn rate > 82% and incident burden (SEV2/SEV3) > 6 hours/day aggregated.

Scope-defer matrix: two axes (customer impact: high/med/low) x (effort: <3pts, 3-8pts, >8pts). Low-impact, low-effort items are deferred first; high-impact, low-effort are elevated for possible fast-track with reserve.
Staffing rotation: each pod sets one float engineer (20% allocation) to act as the reserve consumer; rotates every 3 weeks to spread knowledge and minimize bus factor.
Communication: automated Slack alert to stakeholders when trigger conditions are met, with a pre-populated decision template for PM/Eng lead signoff within 24 hours.
tradeoffs: Holding 10% reserve reduces immediate feature throughput but decreases late-cycle churn and unreleased partially-done work.
Automated trigger avoids manual debate but requires accurate burn and incident telemetry; false positives risk wasting reserve capacity.
Float engineer rotation spreads context but increases ramp overhead; chosen 3-week cadence balances continuity and knowledge distribution.
Conservative reserve (10%) chosen to be non-disruptive; we will iterate if metrics show under/over allocation.
Fast-tracking high-impact items into the reserve increases risk to long-term roadmap work; mitigated via post-cycle capacity reconciliation.
